clue.text: Not over certain what's under monk's hood

indicators.note: over in a down clue tells us to turn the word Not upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: certain means sure

explanation.surface: A hesitant guess at what a monk keeps hidden beneath his cowl.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means upside down, so the word is read bottom to top. The definition is cryptic: the shaved crown is what lies under the hood.
explanation.definitionFit: The shaved patch on a monk's crown is the part of the head that sits beneath the cowl.

clue.text: Reincarcerate on purpose?

explanation.surface: Someone is locked up again, and it was no accident.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as DE-LIBERATE, the word means to undo a freeing, i.e. lock up again; the question mark flags that whimsical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking away liberty again is a whimsical reading of un-freeing; done on purpose means intentional, the everyday adjective.

clue.text: Head right down for upcoming cafe-restaurant -it's a designer thing

indicators.note: the leading letter is shifted all the way to the bottom of the word in this down entry
in a down clue, upcoming means the letters are read from the bottom up

parts.note: taken as written
TRAT is a short informal name for a trattoria, an Italian restaurant

explanation.surface: Advice to a designer on placing a sign for a cafe-restaurant opening soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upcoming' turns CAFE + TRAT into TARTEFAC; 'Head right down' moves its first letter T to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: An artefact is a made object, something designed and crafted by a person.

clue.text: What tree-climber needs to hold?

indicators.note: the hyphenated word is said to hold the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A question about what someone scaling a tree must grip.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits inside 'climber'; and the whole clue is the definition, since a climber grips a branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A branch of a tree is what a person climbing it holds on to.

clue.text: The scramble to succeed, the mark of an artist?

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist
a trace is a mark left behind

explanation.surface: A musing on whether ambition's frantic struggle is what marks out an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: The rat race is the competitive struggle for advancement in working life.

clue.text: Scaremongers smuggling back garden ornament

indicators.note: back says the smuggled run is read from right to left
the long word is carrying a run of letters secretly within it

explanation.surface: Alarmists are caught bringing an ornament for the garden into the country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smuggling' finds EMONG inside Scaremongers; 'back' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: A little bearded statuette is a classic ornament on a lawn or flowerbed.

clue.text: Long look at book of garden construction

parts.note: to gaze is to look long and steadily
O is a short form of of, as in will-o'-the-wisp

explanation.surface: A long look at a gardening book.
explanation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a summer-house or open pavilion built in a garden.

clue.text: Church dignitaries at sixes and sevens?

explanation.surface: Senior churchmen in disarray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sixes and sevens' looks like confusion, but six and seven are cardinal numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Princes of the Roman Catholic Church who elect the Pope; also counting numbers such as six and seven, as opposed to ordinals.

clue.text: Load vehicle and hit the road

parts.note: a car is a vehicle
to hit the road is to go, set off

explanation.surface: Pack up the car and set off on a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Cargo is goods carried, a load in a ship or vehicle.

clue.text: Donkey caught by Spaniard? -he's fuming

indicators.note: the second piece is held within the first, as if trapped

parts.note: SR is short for senor, a Spanish gentleman
a moke is a slang word for a donkey

explanation.surface: A Spaniard grabs a donkey and the creature is livid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught by' puts MOKE inside SR, the abbreviation of Senor; 'fuming' is not anger but tobacco smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: A person puffing a cigarette gives off fumes, so one who smokes is fuming in the literal sense.

clue.text: Final letter causes couple finally to row with more vigour

parts.note: Z is the last letter of the alphabet

indicators.note: the final couple of letters of the word causes are taken

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A rule of rowing that a Z forces pairs to pull harder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'couple finally' takes the last two letters of 'causes', ES.
explanation.definitionFit: Zesty means full of energy and gusto, so its comparative is more energetic.

clue.text: Ring snatch — Crosophile's back in restraint

indicators.note: back here turns the whole string of three pieces round

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
to snatch is to grab
Crosophile is the setter, who refers to himself as ME

explanation.surface: A setter's snatched ring is returned under restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: O + GRAB + ME read backwards gives the answer. Crosophile is the setter's pseudonym, so it gives ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban or restriction, especially on trade.

clue.text: City bank's collateral with church before dodgy loan

indicators.note: before puts the church letters ahead of the rearranged word for the loan

parts.note: a bar is a ridge alongside a bank, as a sandbar runs collateral to a shore
CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: dodgy suggests the word loan is unsound and rearranged

parts.note: the word loan is the material to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A bank's security for a dodgy loan, with a church thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank' and 'collateral' look financial; the bar is a sandbar. 'dodgy' rearranges LOAN into LONA.
explanation.definitionFit: Barcelona is the capital city of Catalonia in Spain.

clue.text: Some proficiency clearly needed on this?

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Skill is obviously required to ride a bicycle.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a hint that riding a bike takes skill, with the run straddling proficienCY CLEarly.
explanation.definitionFit: A bike is something that needs skill to ride, as the surface implies.

clue.text: Protective layer of postman's uniform?

explanation.surface: Armour, or what the letter carrier wears.
explanation.walkthrough: The mail is chain armour, but the question mark invites the postal sense of mail.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain armour worn as body protection, and jokingly a jacket for one delivering post.

clue.text: My ornate headgear incorporates a sample of taffeta

indicators.note: the headgear takes something into its body

parts.note: an ornate headgear is a fancy hat

indicators.note: a sample takes just the opening letter of the fabric word

explanation.surface: An admirer's elaborate hat has a bit of silk taffeta woven in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' looks possessive but is the exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are exclamations of surprise, as in 'Well I never!'

clue.text: Climber, about fifty, not wild about Iceland

parts.note: C is short for circa, about
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: the second about turns the word for not wild round

parts.note: not wild means tame
IS is the international code for Iceland

explanation.surface: A mountaineer around fifty who is not keen on Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Climber' suggests a mountaineer but is a climbing plant. The second 'about' turns TAME into EMAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Clematis is a climbing plant, often grown up walls and trellises.

clue.text: The sound of sea on sea churning vast amounts of water

indicators.note: churning stirs these letters up into a new order
the word sea said out loud sounds like a single letter

parts.note: sea when spoken sounds like the letter C

explanation.surface: The roar of waves breaking over waves on a churning sea.
explanation.walkthrough: C (from 'The sound of sea') plus ON and SEA are churned together.
explanation.definitionFit: The great seas covering the globe hold enormous quantities of water.

clue.text: Like an easy clue?: First of speakers gets loquacious, but not very

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the word speakers
V is short for very, and not very removes it

parts.note: voluble means talkative, loquacious

explanation.surface: A speaker becomes chatty but only mildly so.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not very' drops V (very) from VOLUBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clue that is easy can be solved, and solvable is the meaning given here.

clue.text: This might be colourful over the top round a bit of nosh

definitions.text: This might be colourful over the top round a bit of nosh

indicators.note: round says the first word goes about the second piece

parts.note: garish means gaudy, too brightly coloured

indicators.note: a bit takes just the first letter of nosh

explanation.surface: A description of decoration placed around a plate of food.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a sprig placed on a dish is decoration around food. 'nosh' is British slang for food.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative trimming added to food to make it look attractive.

clue.text: Church official's holding company — another one?

indicators.note: the official's title holds the company inside it

parts.note: a dean is a senior church official; the 's means has

explanation.surface: A church official is in charge of a firm and wonders about another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another one' points back to 'Church official'.
explanation.definitionFit: A deacon is a church officer ranking below a priest, so another clergy officer like a dean.

clue.text: Near the end

explanation.surface: Almost at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearby, said with a hard S; and the conclusion, as in the close of play.

clue.text: Make more of a bundle over zero levy

indicators.note: over says the bundle word is flipped back to front

parts.note: a bale is a bundle, as of hay
O is zero
a rate is a levy or local tax

explanation.surface: Fuss over a bundle of nothing and a tax demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To elaborate is to develop or expand on something in detail.

clue.text: Academy hospital unit gets grant

parts.note: a ward is a unit in a hospital

explanation.surface: A teaching hospital department receives funding.
explanation.definitionFit: To award is to give or bestow, much as a sum is given officially.

clue.text: Acceleration in capacity of returnable gas tanks

parts.note: A is the symbol for acceleration in physics
qua is Latin meaning in the capacity of

indicators.note: returnable says the gas word comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: air is a gas mixture

explanation.surface: A technical note on refillable gas cylinders and how fast they fill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returnable' turns AIR to RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Glass tanks for keeping fish and other water creatures.

clue.text: Bloody unusual

explanation.surface: A slangy exclamation of surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody' looks like a British intensifier, but it describes underdone meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Underdone steak is red and juicy; and not often found.

clue.text: Annual charity receives cut by adult before May returns

indicators.note: cut trims the last letter off the charity word

parts.note: alms are charitable gifts

indicators.note: returns says the word for may is read backwards

parts.note: may in the sense of being permitted means can

explanation.surface: A charity receives a reduced grant from an adult before May comes round again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' shortens ALMS to ALM; 'returns' turns CAN into NAC. 'May' looks like the month but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual book published each year with a calendar and information.

clue.text: Output of local star — very fat-gaining success

parts.note: so means very

indicators.note: the fat word gains the success word inside it

parts.note: lard is fat
a win is a success

explanation.surface: A celebrity becomes very fat after a winning streak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'local star' sounds like a celebrity but is the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: The stream of charged particles flowing outward from the Sun.

clue.text: Children's author's aborted comeback as playwright

indicators.note: comeback says the letters are read backwards
aborted cuts short the name, taking off its last letter

parts.note: E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children

explanation.surface: A children's writer's failed comeback attempt as a dramatist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aborted' cuts NESBIT to NESBI and 'comeback' turns it round. Edith Nesbit was an English children's author.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian dramatist of A Doll's House.
